memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: These were the Israelites who came out of Egypt: The descendants of Reuben, the firstborn son of Israel, were: through Hanoch, the Hanochite clan; through Pallu, the Palluite clan; through Hezron, the Hezronite clan; through Karmi, the Karmite clan. These were the clans of Reuben; those numbered were 43,730. - Num 26:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here begins the long listing of Israel's tribes and clans, family by family. To us these names may seem hard to read and easy to skip. Yet God had each one recorded. These were real people, real families, each known and counted by the Lord. Reuben's descendants are named clan by clan, remembered in God's book.

There is quiet comfort in this careful counting. God does not deal with His people as a faceless crowd. He knows them by name, by family, by clan. Every ordinary person in that vast multitude mattered to Him. The God of heaven took note of each one.

This tells us something about God's character. He is not distant or indifferent to individuals. The same care He showed in counting Israel's families He shows toward each of His children. You are not lost in the crowd to God; you are known and counted, precious in His sight.

The Lord who recorded these ancient names knows your name too. In Christ, God calls His own by name and writes them in the Lamb's book of life (Luke 10:20). You are not overlooked or forgotten. The God who remembered every clan of Israel remembers you, and holds you securely in His love.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe God knows you personally, by name?
2. How does God's careful counting of Israel's families comfort you?
3. What does it mean that your name is known to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that I am not lost in the crowd to You. You know me by name and hold me in Your care. Help me rest in the truth that I am counted and remembered in Christ. Amen.
